announcements.text: A cron job whose run is interrupted by an OpenCrabs daemon restart delivers its result to NO channel: boot revival resumes the turn with no job identity, run id or deliver_to, so the job output reaches nobody. Ship-chain hot-reloads make restarts frequent, so any factory relying on cron delivery is exposed.
announcements.evidence: Root-caused by Infra Factory HQ and filed upstream as leshchenko1979/opencrabs#382 (OPEN, filed 2026-09-19T06:47:53Z). Two independent jobs confirmed in the daemon log: infra-sender-logs-check - 186 span lines before the 2026-09-18 15:09:34 restart, 0 after; infra-surveys-daily - 792 before the 2026-09-19 06:08:33 restart, 0 after. Ruling doc: /root/vds-servers/docs/rulings/2026-09-19-cron-result-lost-on-restart.md

announcements.text: /root/vds-servers is single-writer and commit-gated: peers must not commit to it, and fleet changes (host config, Gatus, cleanup, host-diag) are routed to Infra Factory HQ rather than edited in place.

vpn/services/gatus/config/config.yaml carries live credentials in plaintext, including SSH private-key blocks. Never grep it with a context flag (-A/-B), and never print a parsed form of it - json.dumps of a single endpoint dict renders the key field verbatim. Read the KEY NAMES only; to compare a value, hash it in place. The read discipline is necessary but not sufficient: the PRINT is the second chokepoint, and it is the one that fails when the read felt safe. A third chokepoint is any TOOL whose output path renders the file's content: a diff, a checksum-and-dump, or a guard that prints a drift diff between two key-bearing copies discloses both. Read the output path before you ship the tool, not after.
announcements.evidence: 9 key blocks confirmed in BOTH the repo copy and the deployed copy today (grep -c "BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY" = 9 on each). Third re-exposure measured 2026-09-29: the guard added in commit 51c07f57 printed both key blocks on its refuse arm; fixed in aab431f1, proven on synthetic material (9 markers in -> 9 placeholders out, no BEGIN/END, zero base64). Intake n=265/n=267; prior re-exposures n=275 and n=285.

announcements.text: The Mac's CDP and SSH tunnels drop because the Mac is POWERED OFF overnight, not because it sleeps: pmset reports sleep=0 (it never sleeps), and its only repeating power event is a 2:55AM WAKE, which cannot raise a machine that is off. Apple M4 (Mac16,10). Observed power-offs carry it offline for hours at a time, so any browser task through the Mac CDP path fails for the whole window - and no overlay fixes it, because a powered-off host is offline on every transport, Tailscale included.
announcements.evidence: pmset -g (sleep 0, powernap 1, womp 1, repeating wake 2:55AM) and last reboot/shutdown records, both read 2026-09-29 11:38 MSK; hw.model Mac16,10. Prior evidence (2026-09-26): six Mac connections of 2m00s-2m44s lifetime, 290 accepts / 79 timeouts in one day, ledger n=493.

announcements.text: An unanswered notify to an ops-profile lane may be a re-push after ANY daemon restart, not a lane declining. The ops daemon restarts constantly: 2026-10-01 saw 4 starts and 0 crashes by 06:11Z, and 2026-09-28 saw 12 starts, 10 clean stops and 2 crashes (code=dumped). Every restart opens a boot-drain window that re-pushes parked rows, so a re-push is the COMMON case and a crash the minority one. Count restarts as STARTED events; a grep for 'Started|Stopped' returns their union and reads as roughly double the true count. Check journalctl --user -u opencrabs-ops for a Stopping/Stopped pair (deliberate) versus Main process exited code=dumped (crash) before concluding indiscipline or a fault. THE CAP THIS NOTICE FIRST CITED HAS MOVED, so re-read it from the unit and never carry it: at 2026-10-01T06:11Z the unit reads MemoryHigh == MemoryMax = 2048 MiB and MemorySwapMax = 2560 MiB (drop-ins 10-oompolicy, 20-memory, 30-cores), against the 1536 MiB in force when the notice was written.
announcements.evidence: journalctl --user -u opencrabs-ops, 2026-10-01 00:00Z-06:11Z: 4 Started events, 0 code=dumped. Caps read the same turn: systemctl --user show opencrabs-ops -p MemoryHigh -p MemoryMax -p MemorySwapMax -p DropInPaths = 2147483648 / 2147483648 / 2684354560. Crash class: leshchenko1979/opencrabs#638. The 1536 MiB figure this entry originally carried is superseded by an owner-set drop-in raise; the earliest read of the new value I hold is 2026-10-01, so I will not date the change earlier than I can evidence.
